hero.title: We build open-source infrastructure for businesses.
hero.description: At Opensya, we build open-source infrastructure for businesses. Solid technological foundations designed to meet organizations’ real needs, support their growth, and empower them to build their own solutions. We believe the tools businesses rely on should not be black boxes, but infrastructure that anyone can understand, adapt, and evolve freely.
hero.highlight: We want to give businesses the freedom to build without limits. Open, modular, and sustainable technologies that let them stay in control of their tools, data, and digital future. Because innovation should not depend on imposed solutions, we create the foundations businesses can use to develop, connect, and grow their own ideas. Opensya does more than build software: we build what enables others to build.

meta.title: Authen — Open-source identity and authentication infrastructure | Opensya
meta.description: Authen is an identity and authentication infrastructure project, independent of frameworks and sign-in methods, designed to serve multiple applications.

hero.title: One identity. Multiple applications. The freedom to choose.
hero.intro: Every new application brings its own accounts, sign-in flows, and rules. Authen is an open-source infrastructure project that aims to make identity a shared foundation, independent of frameworks and authentication methods.
hero.tagline: One identity. Any application. Any authentication provider.

problem.title: When every application has its own identity
problem.p1: A person has one account here and another there, and must enter the same information everywhere. Each team rebuilds its own sign-in flow with its own choices, and changing authentication methods means updating every application.
problem.p2: With just one application, this may go unnoticed. As soon as several applications need to work together, identity stops being a sign-in detail and becomes an architectural concern.

approach.title: Separating what should be separate
approach.intro: Authen starts with a simple idea: identity infrastructure is more than a sign-in form. The project therefore separates several concepts that are often conflated.

identity.title: Identity
identity.description: Who the person is, regardless of the application they use.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: Information about the person, which may vary from one context to another.

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.description: How the person proves who they are. This method can change without changing their identity.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.description: The period for which access is granted, and to which application.

approach.principles: Two principles guide the design around this separation: independence from any framework, stack, or authentication method, and extensibility, so new providers can be added without rethinking the whole system. Authen is open source under the Apache 2.0 license.

building.title: What we aim to build
building.intro: Authen is designed as independent infrastructure that can be used by Opensya Workspace and other applications.

items.shared: An identity that can be used across multiple applications.
items.login: Unified sign-in experiences and, eventually, single sign-on (SSO) scenarios.
items.methods: Multiple authentication methods: email and password, codes or links sent by email, phone, and external providers.

state.description: Authen is being designed and developed. The authentication methods and scenarios described above reflect the project’s goals; we do not present them as operational until they are documented in the repository.

closing.title: A foundation built in the open
closing.description: If digital identity for organizations interests you, you can explore and discuss the project and, as it progresses, contribute to it.

meta.title: Workspace — An open, modular work environment | Opensya
meta.description: Workspace is a digital work environment project that aims to bring an organization’s essential tools together in a coherent, open, and modular system.

hero.title: A workspace designed around your organization.
hero.intro: Calendars, notes, messages, video calls, and forms: everyday work relies on tools designed separately. Workspace aims to bring them together in a coherent, modular environment that the organization remains in control of.

problem.title: Tools that don’t talk to each other
problem.p1: A meeting is scheduled in one tool, prepared in another, and followed up in a third. Each has its own accounts, permissions, and administration.
problem.p2: Each tool may be excellent on its own. Bringing them together takes time, attention, and compromises—and the organization bears the cost.

approach.title: Why a new work environment?
approach.intro: Many tools already exist, and many are excellent. Workspace explores a different approach: a system designed from the outset to work coherently, adapt to the organization, and give it greater control over its tools.

open.title: Openness
open.description: A project people can read, understand, and evolve.

modular.title: Modularity
modular.description: Components that adapt to needs, rather than the other way around.

coherent.title: Consistency
coherent.description: A seamless experience from one tool to another.

control.title: Control
control.description: An organization that remains in control of its digital environment.

approach.origin: The idea grew out of the needs of African businesses, particularly in Senegal, but is intended to serve organizations far beyond the region.

building.title: The scope we envision
building.intro: These are the areas Workspace aims to cover. This is the intended scope, not a list of available features.
building.outro: The goal is not to place applications side by side, but to make them work together.

state.description: Workspace is under development. Its scope and capabilities will evolve as it is built, and we do not claim that all planned applications already exist or are currently connected.

closing.title: A work environment shaped in the open
closing.description: If you’re interested in how organizations work and choose their tools, explore the project or talk with us about its direction.

meta.title: One RH — A modular HR platform | Opensya
meta.description: One RH is a human resources management platform project built around a shared core and modules that can evolve with the organization.

hero.title: HR that supports business growth.
hero.intro: Teams grow, processes change, and needs become clearer. One RH is an HR platform project that aims to structure HR management around a shared foundation and modules that can evolve with the organization.

problem.title: HR evolves faster than its tools
problem.p1: As an organization grows, HR processes accumulate one by one, often informally. Team information becomes scattered, and every new need feels like another project to build.
problem.p2: Structuring these processes does not mean freezing them. It means giving them a clear foundation the organization can continue to build on.

approach.title: A shared foundation, modular capabilities
approach.intro: One RH is built on a modular TypeScript architecture. Its core, One RH Core, provides a shared foundation. Business capabilities are built on this foundation, so every new need does not become a separate application.

modules.title: Modules
modules.description: Business capabilities added progressively as the organization needs them.

core.title: One RH Core
core.description: The shared foundation on which the modules rely.

approach.outro: This reflects a core belief: an HR product should evolve gradually, at the pace of the teams it supports.

building.title: What One RH aims to make possible

processes.title: Structure processes
processes.description: Provide a clear framework for how the organization works.

information.title: Organize information
information.description: Bring team-related information together in one place.

evolve.title: Evolve the tools
evolve.description: Add capabilities as needs arise, without starting from scratch.

state.description: One RH is under development. We do not present its modules as complete or the platform as commercially available. No adoption figures or pricing are being claimed.

closing.title: A product that grows with its needs
closing.description: If you’re interested in structuring HR processes and products that evolve gradually, explore the project or talk with us about its direction.

thesis.title: Why these projects, and why now

thesis.p2: Opensya takes a different approach: open, modular infrastructure that businesses can build on and remain in control of.

meta.title: Leadership — Mamadou DIA, Founder of Opensya | Opensya
meta.description: Mamadou DIA, founder and technical lead at Opensya: his approach to engineering, open source, and building sustainable products.

hero.name: Mamadou DIA
hero.role: Founder and Technical Lead at Opensya
hero.title: Understand the problem first. Build the foundations next.
hero.intro: At Opensya, Mamadou DIA leads technical strategy and development. His work starts from a simple principle: a good system is not the one that does the most, but the one that remains understandable as needs change.

approach.title: An engineering approach
approach.background: A senior developer specializing in the JavaScript and TypeScript ecosystem, Mamadou works across both frontend and backend. He has held technical leadership responsibilities, including codebase organization, code reviews, and mentoring developers.
approach.p1: It starts with the problem. Before choosing a framework or database, he seeks to understand what the organization is really trying to achieve—and what is getting in its way today.
approach.p2: For him, architecture is a way to manage complexity: breaking a system into modular parts that can evolve without forcing changes elsewhere. Every technical decision is judged by the value it brings and the long-term cost it imposes on those who maintain it.
approach.p3: That is why the developer experience matters as much as the user experience: a system that is hard to understand soon becomes hard to evolve. Complexity that adds no real value is a debt best avoided.

work.title: From code to products
work.intro: Existing tools are not always enough. We must also understand their limitations, explore other approaches, and, when there is a genuine need, build the missing tool.

products.title: Infrastructure and products
products.description: Opensya projects designed around real organizational problems.

tools.title: Tools for developers
tools.description: Open-source tools that make development simpler and easier to control.

practice.title: Thinking about the craft
practice.description: Architecture, conventions, and developer experience—all of which shape a product’s lifespan.

work.outro: These are not unrelated ideas. They express the same approach: understand problems deeply, design solid foundations, and build reusable solutions.

openSource.title: Why openness matters
openSource.p1: For Mamadou, open source is about more than publishing code. It is a way to build technology that others can examine, understand, adapt, and evolve.
openSource.p2: In practical terms, an organization that can inspect how its tools work can adapt them to its needs without waiting for others to make decisions on its behalf. Opensya exists to support that freedom to build its own digital environment.
